profile: Freelancer, income varies month to month
in_vivo_code: A fixed commitment makes me nervous
summary_paraphrased: Wants to invest monthly but client payments arrive late; counts tax money as spendable; asks if 'flexible SIP' is real or marketing.
codes: irregular income; fear of fixed commitment; mixing tax money with spendable cash; asking a forum to validate the plan; wants amount flexibility

in_vivo_code: Average monthly income can be misleading
summary_paraphrased: Sets aside tax and business costs first, invests what is left; keeps an emergency buffer because a good month is not a good quarter.
codes: irregular income; separating money into buckets; emergency buffer before investing; control over amount keeps them investing

in_vivo_code: I stopped my SIPs after making the switch
summary_paraphrased: Stopped all SIPs when cash flow became irregular; parks surplus in liquid funds and invests lump sums in falls (e.g. March 2026).
codes: irregular income; stopping SIP after income change; parking money in liquid funds; buying lump sums in market falls; control over amount keeps them investing

profile: Retail investor, mostly stocks, includes MFs in criticism
in_vivo_code: Long term is the biggest scam
summary_paraphrased: Saw holdings swing from +30% to -10%; says Nifty gave 0% since mid-2024; distrusts the 'stay invested' message from AMCs and prefers booking profits.
codes: flat or negative returns; distrust of industry message; booking profits instead of holding; anger at volatility

in_vivo_code: No SIPs, mostly buy on dips
summary_paraphrased: Put lump sums into 8 funds when the index fell; confused about active vs index funds; now plans to trade an index ETF and sell at +5%.
codes: buying lump sums in market falls; too many funds; confused about fund choice; asking a forum to validate the plan; drift from investing to trading

in_vivo_code: kept waiting for a dip
summary_paraphrased: Waited for a dip while the index rose sharply in 2020-21; now believes a plain SIP would have done better.
codes: waiting for a dip; regret after waiting; SIP seen as protection from own timing

in_vivo_code: I missed the train
summary_paraphrased: Held cash waiting for a dip in 2013-14 and missed the rally; that regret now keeps them investing regularly.
codes: waiting for a dip; regret after waiting; past mistake keeps them invested

in_vivo_code: one shouldn't stop SIP waiting for the DIP
summary_paraphrased: Keeps SIPs running in all markets and holds a separate cash pool to add in dips; a fixed equity/debt split guides moves.
codes: keeps SIP running in falls; separating money into buckets; rules replace feelings

profile: Was about to start first SIP
in_vivo_code: I'll stay away from SIP
summary_paraphrased: A WhatsApp-forwarded article convinced them SIPs fail; felt let down by heavy 'MF Sahi Hai' ads; decided not to start.
codes: outside content shapes the decision; misleading return comparisons; distrust of industry message; feels misled by advertising

in_vivo_code: SHOCKED TO LEARN THIS
summary_paraphrased: A third-party SIP calculator showed -30% over 13 years (others in the thread found the calculator was wrong); shock turned into doubt.
codes: return numbers they cannot interpret; misleading return comparisons; shock turns into distrust

in_vivo_code: it's not the SIP to be blamed, it's our mindset
summary_paraphrased: Returns were good until 2018; blames investors' mindset, not SIPs; thinks gains should be moved to safer funds at highs.
codes: keeps SIP running in falls; responsibility on self, not product; wants a rule for taking gains

profile: SIP investor in a gold fund
in_vivo_code: SIP in SBI Gold Fund was being paused
summary_paraphrased: Fund house paused the SIP with a day's notice; they wanted it to continue and were surprised existing SIPs were affected.
codes: SIP stopped by fund house, not investor; surprise at a change they did not choose; asking a forum to explain

in_vivo_code: pause without cancelling
summary_paraphrased: Asks for pause/resume and amount changes on existing SIPs so they never have to cancel and re-register.
codes: wants amount flexibility; wants pause instead of cancel; fear of losing the SIP for good

profile: Started first SIP the day before
in_vivo_code: confused about next sip installment
summary_paraphrased: Cancelled their first SIP order a day after paying because they could not tell when the next instalment would be taken.
codes: unclear payment schedule; cancelling first SIP; confusion ends the SIP before it starts

in_vivo_code: I treated SIP as a magic tool
summary_paraphrased: Opened many overlapping SIPs; checked NAVs daily; in the 2010 fall almost stopped and moved to FDs after press said FDs beat SIPs; books and learning kept them in.
codes: too many funds; checking NAV daily; comparing with FD returns; nearly stopping in a fall; outside content shapes the decision; learning replaces panic

profile: First MF investor in family, started 2008
in_vivo_code: I am thankful I did not quit
summary_paraphrased: Started a small ELSS SIP after family medical debt; returns were near zero for 5+ years; later stopped the SIP mandate because the amount grew, but kept investing manually.
codes: flat or negative returns; goal bigger than returns; stopping SIP form, keeps investing; control over amount keeps them investing

in_vivo_code: And I still feel the pull.
summary_paraphrased: Even as a professional, feels anxiety and the urge to act in falls; says knowledge does not switch off the instinct.
codes: urge to act in a fall; knowledge does not remove fear; keeps SIP running in falls

in_vivo_code: it hit me hard
summary_paraphrased: Felt proud seeing a projected Rs 1 crore, then deflated when inflation cut its real value; keeps the SIP but plans to raise savings with income.
codes: projection pride; inflation shrinks the dream; recalculating projections; plans to step up with income

in_vivo_code: Reacting to someone else's number
summary_paraphrased: Raised SIP to match a friend; six months later a cash crunch forced a pause; felt worse because the amount was never their own choice.
codes: matching a friend's SIP amount; cash crunch; pausing in a cash crunch; social comparison sets the amount

profile: Distributor and planner; SIP for son's education since 2013
in_vivo_code: It can be unnerving, but I reminded myself
summary_paraphrased: Stopped investing in 2008-09 and moved to FDs, later called it a mistake; since 2013 runs a goal SIP and adds money in dips, with yearly reviews.
codes: stopping in a fall, regretted later; comparing with FD returns; goal bigger than returns; keeps SIP running in falls; regret after waiting
